name: Stonehenge construction stages
about: Stonehenge's construction stages, for a stage slider: the earthwork enclosure and Aubrey Holes of c. 3000 BC, the timber settings, the double bluestone arc (Q and R holes), the Station Stones, entrance stones and Heel Stone, the sarsen settings of c. 2500 BC (detailed in stones.json), the bluestone rearrangements, the Avenue and the Y and Z holes of c. 1600 BC, with Darvill et al.'s five stages (2012) as the main scheme and Cleal et al.'s phases (1995, via Lawson 1997), Parker Pearson's revised dates and Wikipedia's and English Heritage's summaries as alternatives. Radii are from the centre of the circles; azimuths are degrees from true north. Quotes are exact text from the cited pages (whitespace normalised; some OCR spellings kept as they appear). 'derived' marks values computed from quoted numbers, read off a plan or measured from OpenStreetMap features against the existing model's sarsen ring centre.

Darvill et al. say the entrance was later modified to give a symmetrical gap either side of the principal axis (49.57 deg, Lockyer and Penrose, in stones.json); Parker Pearson et al. say the Stage 1 entrance was also aligned broadly on the northernmost major moonrise (compute its azimuth with bidb.sky / static/sky.js for 3000 BC).

aubrey_centre.value: same centre as the enclosure (Lawson); offset from the sarsen circle's centre about 2.9 m towards azimuth about 146 deg (derived, weak)
aubrey_centre.note: Lawson: the Aubrey circle shares the enclosure's centre; Lockyer (1909): the sarsen circle is concentric with the earthwork ('temenos mound'). Derived check: a 43.2 m circle fitted to the seven OSM Aubrey Hole markers (26-32, an arc of about 40 deg in the south-west) has its centre 1.6 m east and 2.4 m south of the sarsen ring centre (2.9 m at 146 deg; with r 42.7-43.7 m the centre moves 1.2-2.0 m E, 2.1-2.7 m S). The four Station Stones (on the Aubrey line) give a rectangle centred 3.1 m at 143 deg from the sarsen centre, which agrees. A short arc constrains the centre poorly; the offset is a pointer, not a measurement. Thom's published offset (about 1.5 megalithic yards along the axis) was seen only on forum pages and is not used.

gaps: Cleal, Walker & Montague 1995 (Stonehenge in its Landscape) is not online (not on archive.org; Historic England's copy is behind Cloudflare); its plans 1-2 and Figs 68, 81-82 hold the surveyed positions of every Aubrey, Q/R and Y/Z hole and the A posts. Lawson 1997 (its summary) is used instead.
Petrie 1880 is not on archive.org (searched once; nothing found). Atkinson's Stonehenge (1956, 1979) is on archive.org only as a borrow-only (access-restricted) scan; only his 1967 guide is readable.

No source gives the azimuths of the NE and S entrances or the third entrance's position: NE about 44 deg and S about 177 deg are read off Adamsan's schematic plan (derived). Hawley's segment numbering (which would place segments 17-18 and 21-23) was not found.

The offset between the Aubrey/enclosure centre and the sarsen circle's centre is not stated in any reachable source; Lawson and Lockyer say they share a centre. The derived 2.9 m (OSM markers of seven holes) is weak; Thom's figure was found only on forum pages.
Positions of single Aubrey Holes beyond 26-32, of Q/R settings, of stoneholes B, C, D, E and of the A posts are not in any reachable open source; only the counts, radii and spacings are.
Counterscarp bank width and height, Avenue bank and ditch widths and depths, and Y/Z hole positions one by one were not found.
Lawson's figures for the Aubrey Holes' own size (about 1 m across, 0.9 m deep) are garbled by OCR in the British Academy PDF and are not quoted; Wikipedia's averages (1.06 m, 0.76 m) are used.
Hawley's reports (Antiquaries Journal 1921-1928) are on Cambridge Core as first pages only; the transcription site found by search (twentytrees.co.uk) answers HTTP 410.

Parker Pearson et al. 2009 ('Who was buried at Stonehenge?', Antiquity 83) and 2020 (Stonehenge for the Ancestors part 1) were not opened; their revised dates are quoted as cited in Parker Pearson et al. 2021-2022.

Darvill et al.'s stage plans (Figs 3-8) and Marshall et al. 2012 (English Heritage Research Report 1/2012) are not openly licensed; the Historic England research report site was not tried (it refuses scripts).
